title: The One With Monicas Thunder

jokes.text: Note says 'Come to Monica's. Bring champagne and a Three Musketeers bar'
jokes.setup: Ross reads a mysterious note left on his door instructing him to bring specific items
jokes.punchline: The oddly specific pairing of celebratory champagne with a candy bar immediately signals Monica's particular personality — the note is so her
jokes.explanation: The joke works through character specificity — Monica's controlling, food-obsessed nature is efficiently communicated through one absurd note. The candy bar next to champagne is a small but effective laugh.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm engaged!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wait, you're gay?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, I'm ENGAGED!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Right, right, I heard you the first time.

jokes.text: "She's been there for 20 minutes. You didn't hear?" / "I thought it was a kid yelling, 'I'm gay!'"
jokes.setup: Chandler asks if Joey heard Monica screaming her engagement news from the balcony
jokes.punchline: Joey misheard 'I'm engaged' as 'I'm gay,' recontextualizing her shouting as a coming-out moment
jokes.explanation: Tight misdirection with excellent economy. The phonetic similarity between 'engaged' and 'gay' is genuinely clever, the visual of a child shouting 'I'm gay' adds absurdist color, and Joey's earnest delivery would make it land perfectly. One of the episode's cleaner joke constructions.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: There was.

jokes.text: Monica, still on the balcony: 'Oh, big talk! Why don't you come here and say that to me?'
jokes.setup: Monica has been joyfully screaming her engagement news for 20 minutes; apparently a neighbor told her to shut up
jokes.punchline: Monica's celebration has escalated into a shouting confrontation with a stranger, fully consistent with her aggressive personality
jokes.explanation: Strong character integration — Monica turning a joy-scream into a street fight is perfectly on-brand. The joke earns its laugh through the absurd escalation of the situation rather than a sharp line.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm engaged! I'm engaged!

dialogue.speaker: Neighbor
dialogue.line: Some of us are trying to sleep!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, some of us are getting married!

jokes.text: "My fiancé will kick your ass."
jokes.setup: Monica is in a shouting match with an unseen neighbor from the balcony
jokes.punchline: She weaponizes her new engagement status as a threat, immediately drafting Chandler into her street beef
jokes.explanation: Extremely economical. Five words that do triple duty: they're funny on their own, they escalate the balcony bit to absurdity, and they're a perfect Monica character moment. Chandler being immediately deployed as muscle is quietly hilarious.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You want to mess with me? I've got Chandler!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Why would you say that?

jokes.text: "You get her in, you bolt the door, I'll be in the closet."
jokes.setup: Monica has challenged an unseen neighbor to a physical confrontation from the balcony
jokes.punchline: Chandler's fight-or-flight response is immediately to hide in the closet, undercutting Monica's threat and his own status as her protector
jokes.explanation: Perfect character-consistent callback. Chandler's cowardice is a well-established trait, and his tactical planning to hide in a closet while Monica fights reads as both funny and very true to the character. The military-style logistics delivery adds deadpan charm.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could I BE any more terrified of Monica right now?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm just gonna slowly back away and pretend I don't know her.

jokes.text: "Our special night. / It just wouldn't be my night... Our night... / ...if you weren't here to celebrate with me... Us. Damn it!"
jokes.setup: Monica is making a heartfelt toast at her engagement gathering
jokes.punchline: She keeps slipping from 'our' back to 'my,' revealing that despite genuinely loving Chandler, she privately thinks of this as her night — the self-correction escalates to an exasperated 'Damn it!'
jokes.explanation: Excellent character-integrated cringe comedy. The slippage from 'my' to 'our' and back is perfectly constructed — it escalates naturally and the final 'Damn it!' is an honest moment of self-awareness that makes the audience love Monica even as they laugh at her. High character integration score because this joke only works for Monica specifically.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I want to thank everyone who helped make this day special. Rachel, for being my best friend. Phoebe, for your wonderful songs. Joey, for... well, for being Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What about me?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: And Chandler, of course! And Ross, my brother, who walked me down the aisle.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm already forgotten?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No! I also want to thank the amazing caterer, the photographer, the florist...

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Monica!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What?! Oh my God, and Chandler! How could I forget Chandler, my wonderful husband!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: And I especially want to thank my parents for their support, and my bridesmaids who looked absolutely beautiful...

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Are you kidding me right now?

jokes.text: Phoebe immediately pivots from the toast to asking about the wedding band because she's 'kind of musical'
jokes.setup: Everyone raises a glass to toast Monica at her engagement celebration
jokes.punchline: Phoebe immediately uses the emotional moment to audition herself as the wedding band, framing her self-interest as a casual aside
jokes.explanation: Classic Phoebe — obliviously self-serving while believing she's being helpful. The 'kind of musical' understatement is a nice touch. Functional character comedy, not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I could play music at your wedding!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's so sweet, but... remember when your apartment caught on fire?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: That was ONE time!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Exactly. I'd like my wedding to be ONE time too.

jokes.text: "Speaking of chiming in, remember burning my apartment?"
jokes.setup: Someone (likely Ross) comments on Phoebe inappropriately chiming in
jokes.punchline: Ross uses 'speaking of chiming in' to pivot to reminding someone they burned his apartment, connecting the two via biting sarcasm
jokes.explanation: The pivot construction ('speaking of chiming in') is clever, but without full context of whose apartment burned and why, the punchline lands as a solid if unremarkable callback to off-screen history.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I need to look good for this audition. They're looking for someone who can play 19.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, you're gonna need a time machine.

jokes.text: "So when you said get up early, did you mean 1986?"
jokes.setup: Joey says he needs to get up early for an audition where he's playing a 19-year-old and needs to look good
jokes.punchline: Chandler implies Joey last looked 19 in 1986 — a sharp age joke delivered with his trademark timing
jokes.explanation: Economical and sharp. The 1986 specificity makes it funnier than a generic 'you're old' joke would be. Chandler's delivery would amplify it. Clean construction: setup creates vulnerability, punchline exploits it efficiently.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Do you think I look 19?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: 90? Yeah, sure, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Nineteen? No way. You look way older than that.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Yeah, definitely not 19.

jokes.text: "Oh, 19! We thought you said 90."
jokes.setup: Joey sincerely asks if the group thinks he looks 19
jokes.punchline: Ross pretends they misheard '19' as '90,' suggesting Joey looks elderly rather than merely middle-aged
jokes.explanation: Competent pile-on joke after Chandler's sharper version. The '90' gag is simpler and more obvious than the 1986 line, but works as escalation. It's the second punch at the same target, which diminishes its impact relative to the first.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Look at this ring! It's absolutely gorgeous.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You know what would be perfect? Diamond shoes to match!

jokes.text: "Is my candy bar around here?" / "No, you ate it all." / "I was afraid of that."
jokes.setup: In the midst of engagement celebration, Monica looks for her Three Musketeers bar
jokes.punchline: She already ate the entire candy bar and her response ('I was afraid of that') is resigned self-awareness rather than surprise
jokes.explanation: Pays off the opening candy bar setup with a satisfying callback. 'I was afraid of that' is a beautifully understated line — Monica's compulsive eating is a core character trait and the deadpan resignation is funnier than any exaggerated reaction would be.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Fashion is about youth.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Fashion is about me?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, youth!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh, okay.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Come on, Grandpa.

jokes.text: "You know what shoes would look great with this ring? Diamond shoes."
jokes.setup: Monica is admiring her new engagement ring
jokes.punchline: She leaps directly to 'diamond shoes' — an absurdly extravagant pairing that reveals her maximalist fantasy of wealth
jokes.explanation: Funny in its simplicity. The jump from 'shoes' (reasonable) to 'diamond shoes' (absurd) is fast and confident. Good economy — it's one line, it paints Monica's aspirational materialism, and it gets out quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: It's okay, it happens to a lot of guys.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, it's never happened to me before. I failed biology in high school, but biology never failed me.

jokes.text: "Chandler, it happens to lots of guys." / "You're tired, you had a lot of champagne. Don't worry about it." / "I'm not worried. I'm fascinated."
jokes.setup: Monica comforts Chandler about an apparent bedroom failure on their engagement night using the standard reassuring platitudes
jokes.punchline: Chandler reframes his erectile dysfunction not as embarrassment but as intellectual curiosity — 'I'm fascinated' — a quintessentially Chandler neurotic deflection
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. 'I'm not worried. I'm fascinated.' subverts the expected shame response in a way that is wholly specific to Chandler's intellectualizing, deflecting personality. The twist from vulnerable to detached-academic is sharp and original. The structure is perfect: Monica's sympathetic setup (which we've heard a hundred times) makes the left-field punchline land harder. High character integration because this response could only come from Chandler.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, I'd love to sing at your wedding! I have the perfect song. It's called 'Monica Geller Had a Messy Apartment' to the tune of 'The Star-Spangled Banner.'

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Phoebe, no.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh come on, it's beautiful! 'Oh say can you see, all the stuff piled up to the ceiling, with your mother's obsession and your need for perfection, your apartment's a time bomb that's—'

jokes.text: "It's like biology. Which is funny, because in high school I failed biology... ...and tonight biology failed me."
jokes.setup: Chandler is processing his erectile dysfunction by intellectualizing it as a biological phenomenon
jokes.punchline: He constructs a callback to failing high school biology — 'and tonight biology failed me' — turning his sexual failure into a symmetrical cosmic joke
jokes.explanation: This is the episode's standout line. The parallel construction 'I failed biology / biology failed me' is genuinely clever wordplay with a perfect internal rhythm. It's quotable, it's character-specific (Chandler's self-deprecating wit used to process humiliation), and the structural symmetry is satisfying. This is professional-grade comedy writing — not quite legendary but clearly excellent.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, I thought you were gay. But then I realized you were just metrosexual. You're very well groomed and you have a skincare routine. But then I realized you were just British!

jokes.text: Phoebe's song: "First time I met Chandler I thought he was gay / But here I am singing on his wedding day"
jokes.setup: Phoebe has been auditioning herself to sing at the wedding; she plays an original song
jokes.punchline: The opening lyric of her 'wedding song' is that she initially thought the groom was gay — a wildly inappropriate choice for a wedding number delivered with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: Classic Phoebe song comedy. The joke works because she's genuinely trying to write a beautiful wedding song and is oblivious to how inappropriate 'I thought he was gay' is as an opening lyric. The earnestness amplifies the absurdity. Her follow-up defense ('it goes on to say he's probably not gay') makes it even better.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, well, the song does say at the end that he's probably not gay.

jokes.text: "Phoebe, no." / "If you'd let me finish, it goes on to say that he's probably not gay."
jokes.setup: Chandler objects to Phoebe's wedding song opening about thinking he was gay
jokes.punchline: Phoebe defends the song by clarifying it goes on to say he's 'probably' not gay — the qualifier 'probably' making the reassurance worse than the insult
jokes.explanation: The word 'probably' is doing all the heavy lifting here and it's doing it brilliantly. Phoebe genuinely believes she's defending herself, but 'probably not gay' is functionally worse than 'I thought he was gay.' This is a one-word joke that demonstrates exceptional economy and character integration — only Phoebe, through total obliviousness, could make this escalation feel natural.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You know what the worst part about having erectile dysfunction is? It's not the obvious thing. It's that you're standing there with a beautiful woman, and all you can think about is wooden furniture. Because at least the furniture gets to be hard.

jokes.text: "You guys don't have this problem, you're made of wood."
jokes.setup: Chandler, frustrated by the song about his sexual failure, looks at Monica's wooden furniture or decor
jokes.punchline: He enviously addresses inanimate wooden objects for not having to deal with erectile dysfunction
jokes.explanation: A charming absurdist aside. The joke's funniest dimension is that it implies Chandler has been silently envying wooden furniture. Reasonably funny but relatively lightweight — the visual of Chandler talking to furniture does a lot of the work.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, let's see how long that lasts.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I give it... three years? Maybe four if they really work at it.

jokes.text: Joey reacting to something — "Hey, you look great. / Thanks. / You okay over there? / I don't know. You know? I feel a little..." (trails off)
jokes.setup: Joey approaches Rachel, who appears visibly off — she's been struggling with her feelings about Monica's engagement
jokes.punchline: Rachel trails off mid-sentence, unable or unwilling to articulate what she's feeling, creating an uncomfortable beat
jokes.explanation: Transitional moment more than a full joke. The comedic element is the awkward trailing off, but it's primarily setup for later emotional beats rather than a laugh in its own right. Functional but weak as a standalone comedic moment.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Do you think we'll ever have what Monica and Chandler have?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh God, no.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Yeah, me neither.

jokes.text: "Well, sure, but I get married all the time."
jokes.setup: Someone marvels that Monica and Chandler are actually getting married
jokes.punchline: Ross, who has been divorced three times, responds as if marriage is a casual, frequent occurrence for him — treating his disastrous romantic history as a mundane hobby
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's sharpest lines. The deadpan 'I get married all the time' reframes Ross's three failed marriages as a casual lifestyle rather than a tragedy. Perfect economy — five words to get a big laugh using deep character knowledge. Only works because the audience knows Ross's history.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You know what? I'm actually relieved we're not together anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Really? Me too.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah, I mean, our relationship was a nightmare. Do you know how many times I had to explain paleontology to you?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh, please. You were the nightmare. You were always so... so Ross.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So Ross?! That's not even an insult!

jokes.text: Ross and Rachel's 'bonus night' conversation: "Do you think we'll ever have that?" / "You mean 'we,' you and me?" / "Oh, no, no, no." / "Good, you scared me a minute." / "I know. Shake it off."
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel watch Monica and Chandler's engagement and Rachel asks if they'll 'ever have that'
jokes.punchline: Ross immediately panics thinking Rachel means them as a couple; Rachel clarifies she means generally; Ross's relieved 'shake it off' is both funny and loaded given their history
jokes.explanation: The joke works on multiple levels: surface comedy of a misread question, plus dramatic irony since the audience knows Ross still has feelings for Rachel. The mutual 'shake it off' as if their history was a bad dream adds a layer of wry self-awareness. Rewatch bonus for the irony that becomes richer knowing where their storyline goes.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: There were some really good times in our relationship.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: ...Yeah?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Like... like when?

jokes.text: Ross and Rachel struggling to name one good thing about their relationship: "No, but there were some good times." / "Absolutely. Like there was..." (long silence) / "Surely you can think of something." / "Just give me a minute."
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel mutually agree their relationship had some good times
jokes.punchline: Neither can actually name one — the extended silence as they rack their brains is the joke
jokes.explanation: The silence IS the joke, and it's well-constructed. The escalating qualifiers ('Surely you can think of something' / 'Just give me a minute') prolong and deepen the discomfort. The audience has watched years of Ross and Rachel drama, so the implication that there's nothing memorable is funnier and more painful than any explicit insult would be.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, the stuff... I mean, we had really great stuff.

jokes.text: The best thing about their relationship Rachel can think of: "You were always good at the... stuff." (long pause) / "I really liked your hands."
jokes.setup: After a long silence, Rachel finally comes up with one good thing about their relationship
jokes.punchline: The best compliment she can offer is an extremely vague '...stuff,' followed by a pivot to 'I really liked your hands' — an oddly specific but deeply unromantic consolation prize
jokes.explanation: The extended pause before 'stuff' is perfect setup. 'Stuff' is a brilliantly vague implication of sexual competence, then 'I really liked your hands' deflates it into something weirdly clinical. Ross's response — 'My hands?' — captures the absurdity of receiving this as a compliment. The whole sequence builds to something funnier than the sum of its parts.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I like your stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I like your hands.

jokes.text: "Yes, on a scale of one to ten, ten being the dumbest a person can look... you are definitely 19."
jokes.setup: Joey emerges from his bedroom in his teenager costume/posture and asks 'Come on, am I 19 or what?'
jokes.punchline: Chandler's scale redefines '19' not as an age but as the maximum level of looking dumb — a clever double meaning that insults Joey while technically answering his question
jokes.explanation: Sharp joke construction. By framing '19' as the highest point on a scale of stupidity, Chandler creates a double-meaning insult: Joey looks 19, and 19 means 'maximally idiotic.' The setup structure ('on a scale of one to ten, ten being...') creates a beat that makes the punchline land harder. One of Chandler's better zingers in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yo, yo, yo! What's up, my man? You got any bling bling? I'm about to go to the club and get jiggy with it!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Okay, first of all, stop talking. Second of all, why are you dressed like you're about to commit a crime? And third of all, if you're here to rob me, I should tell you I have nothing of value except this half-eaten sandwich.

jokes.text: "Young. You're a man-child, okay? Now get changed, everybody's ready. And please, please, keep my underwear."
jokes.setup: Joey is wearing what appears to be teenage-style clothing — apparently including Chandler's underwear — as part of his 19-year-old costume
jokes.punchline: Chandler's exasperated 'keep my underwear' reveals Joey has borrowed his underwear as part of the teenager outfit, an absurd detail played as a weary afterthought
jokes.explanation: The 'keep my underwear' button is a good tag — the specificity of Chandler being resigned to losing his underwear to Joey's costuming scheme is funny and very true to their odd-couple dynamic.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yo, that is totally da bomb, fo' shizzle!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: All that and a bag of chips, am I right?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: That's whack! Totally tight!

jokes.text: "You've had a lot of sex, right?" / "When, today?"
jokes.setup: Chandler awkwardly approaches Joey to ask about sexual experience, trying to get advice about his ED
jokes.punchline: Joey's instant clarifying question 'When, today?' implies he has so much sex that the timeframe is a necessary variable — delivered as a completely sincere question
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes and among the best in Friends overall. The word 'today' is the entire joke — it recontextualizes the question into a world where Joey has so much sex that 'a lot' needs to be temporally specified. The genius is that Joey is 100% sincere: this isn't a boast, it's a genuine need for clarification. Perfect economy (two words do all the work), maximum character integration (absolutely only Joey), and structurally flawless. This is approaching the 8.0 anchor-level quality.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Do I look 19?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah... you look like you're 19 and stupid.

jokes.text: "Well, what'd you do?" / "I did it anyway."
jokes.setup: Chandler asks what Joey did when erectile dysfunction happened to him once
jokes.punchline: Joey's advice is simply 'I did it anyway' — a cheerfully oblivious non-solution delivered as genuine wisdom
jokes.explanation: Four words, enormous laugh. The joke works because Joey genuinely believes 'I did it anyway' is helpful advice — his sexual confidence is so fundamental that he never considered not doing it. The deadpan delivery is crucial. Highly quotable and a perfect character moment: Joey as an oracle of a very specific kind of wisdom.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: How old do I look in these clothes?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, the good news is you look like you're in your thirties. The bad news is you're wearing my underwear.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: So?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So? You can keep them.

jokes.text: Chandler's silent reaction to 'I did it anyway' — presumably staring blankly at Joey
jokes.setup: Joey delivers 'I did it anyway' as genuine life advice
jokes.punchline: Chandler's wordless response — the audience can only see his face — registers the gap between what he needed and what he received
jokes.explanation: The reaction beat extends the laugh from joke #28. Matthew Perry's face would do significant comedy work here. Functional but entirely dependent on the preceding joke's quality.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Have you had a lot of sex?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Today? No, not today.

jokes.text: If you touch my guitar again, I'll have to pound on you a little bit.
jokes.setup: Monica bribes Phoebe by saying she can play at the wedding if she gets ready now
jokes.punchline: She immediately adds a threat: 'if you touch my guitar again, I'll have to pound on you a little bit' — a physical threat delivered as a mild afterthought
jokes.explanation: 'Pound on you a little bit' as a qualified threat is funny — it's both more specific and less threatening than 'I'll hurt you.' Monica's matter-of-fact aggression is a consistent character trait.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, I need your advice about something personal.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Sure, buddy. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, I'm having some... performance issues. In the bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh man, that's rough. But hey, you came to the right guy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Did I? Because you're wearing a backwards tuxedo t-shirt, and that's when I realized I've hit rock bottom.

jokes.text: "If you get ready now, you can play." / "Really?!" / "Yes." / "That's so exciting! Thanks, Mon." / "But if you touch my guitar again, I'll have to pound on you a little bit."
jokes.setup: Monica bribes Phoebe to get ready by promising she can play at the wedding
jokes.punchline: Monica immediately follows her generous promise with a threat to 'pound on' Phoebe if she touches the guitar — revealing the offer was entirely transactional manipulation
jokes.explanation: Monica's controlling nature comes through — she gives and immediately sets conditions. 'Pound on you a little bit' is a funny phrase, oddly specific and threatening. Solid character comedy, nothing exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What did you do when you had erectile dysfunction?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I went ahead anyway.

jokes.text: Monica opens her door and finds Ross and Rachel in a romantic/intimate moment: "I'm sorry, apparently I opened the door to the past."
jokes.setup: Monica walks in on Ross and Rachel in a romantic moment on her engagement night
jokes.punchline: She frames what she's seeing as a literal door to the past — their old relationship — with withering sarcasm delivered at the worst possible moment
jokes.explanation: Smart line. 'The door to the past' is a genuinely witty metaphor for Ross and Rachel's recycled romantic tension. Monica's sarcasm is calibrated perfectly — it's funny without being cruel. Good construction.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You can play guitar at my wedding, but if you mess up, I will kill you. And then I will dig you up and kill you again.

jokes.text: "Maybe it's selfish, I'm sorry, but I hoped tonight could just be about that." / "But it is just about that." / "Now it's about you getting back together." / "See, you kind of stole my thunder."
jokes.setup: Monica confronts Ross and Rachel about ruining her engagement night
jokes.punchline: The formal coining of 'you stole my thunder' as the charge — Monica naming what has happened with maximum injured dignity
jokes.explanation: The 'thunder' metaphor is the episode's title concept, and it's well-deployed here. Monica's indignation is funny, but this moment functions more as plot engine than pure comedy. The joke is in her formal declaration.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God! Oh my God! Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Finally! I've been waiting for this for like ten years!

jokes.text: "You guys kissed?! What does this mean?! Are you back together? Can I sing at your wedding?"
jokes.setup: It comes out that Ross and Rachel kissed; everyone reacts
jokes.punchline: Phoebe processes the emotional news through the lens of her own wedding-singing ambitions, making 'can I sing at your wedding?' the fourth and most absurd question in a rapid-fire sequence
jokes.explanation: The escalating questions work beautifully. The first three (what does this mean, are you back together) are what everyone thinks; the fourth (can I sing) is Phoebe recalibrating a potential romantic catastrophe as a professional opportunity. The pivot is perfectly in character and the rhythm of the four questions sets it up well.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You guys kissed?! That's huge! I was gonna tell everyone at dinner tonight that I'm getting married, and now nobody's gonna care because you two are gonna be all 'We kissed, we kissed!' And nobody's gonna want to hear about my wedding!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Monica, come on, that's not—

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You're stealing my thunder!

jokes.text: Thunder being stolen.
jokes.setup: Everyone is now buzzing about Ross and Rachel's kiss instead of Monica's engagement
jokes.punchline: Monica provides real-time color commentary on what's happening to her: 'Thunder being stolen.' — delivered like a sportscaster narrating her own misfortune
jokes.explanation: Three words, enormous laugh. 'Thunder being stolen' as present-progressive self-commentary is a brilliantly economical joke. Monica narrating her own victimhood in passive voice is both funny and character-perfect. This is the thematic punchline of the episode title delivered as a joke. High quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, oh my God! Did you see that? Ross and Rachel just kissed!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Yeah, I was there. And I'm thrilled for them, I really am. But could they have picked literally any other moment? I just got engaged!

jokes.text: "Oh, my God. I cannot believe you guys are talking about this. Problems in the bedroom are between a man and woman. All right? Now, Chandler is doing the best he can."
jokes.setup: Everyone is talking about Ross and Rachel's kiss
jokes.punchline: Joey dramatically defends 'bedroom privacy'... but misidentifies which couple's bedroom issue is being discussed, inadvertently revealing Chandler's ED to the room
jokes.explanation: Excellent structure. Joey's self-righteous speech about privacy is undercut by the fact that he's simultaneously broadcasting the wrong bedroom secret. The layers here: Joey thinks he's being noble, he's actually exposing Chandler, and he doesn't even realize the conversation was about something else entirely. 'Chandler is doing the best he can' is a brilliantly misguided defense that opens an entire new front of embarrassment.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. You guys are talking about Chandler's sexual problems?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, Joey, we're talking about Ross and Rachel's kiss.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh. So... no sexual problems?

jokes.text: "I don't think that's what they were talking about."
jokes.setup: Joey's impassioned defense of Chandler's bedroom performance to a confused room
jokes.punchline: Ross's quiet, dry correction is the comedic button — the understatement in the face of Joey's oblivious oversharing
jokes.explanation: Classic straight-man button. The line does exactly what it needs to in as few words as possible, but it's a support joke rather than a standalone one.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh, that's great! That's just great! My engagement night is ruined, Chandler's been kidnapped by a runaway bride, and now I'm standing here in this dress that cost more than my first apartment, and nobody even noticed!

jokes.text: "What a great night. Chandler can't do it, they kissed."
jokes.setup: Monica is processing the cumulative chaos of her engagement night
jokes.punchline: She summarizes the evening's disasters with flat resignation — the deadpan inventory of catastrophes on what should be her best night is the joke
jokes.explanation: The flat list structure works well — the comedy is in the compression. 'Chandler can't do it' casually reduces a private sexual problem to a memo item, which is both funny and a little brutal. Monica's deadpan mode is a welcome contrast to her usual intensity.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Come on, Rachel. Do you really think I could pass for 19?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I mean, if I really wanted to, couldn't I pull it off?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Rachel, seriously, be honest with me. Could I pass for 19?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Joey, you're 30 years old.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I know that! I'm asking if I could pass for 19!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No. You look like a man in his thirties who's been through some stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait... how old am I again?

jokes.text: "Would you feel better if we stopped talking about Ross and Rachel?" / "That would be lovely." / "You got it. Now, I can pass for 19, right?"
jokes.setup: Ross tries to redirect conversation away from himself and Rachel to spare Monica
jokes.punchline: Joey immediately pivots to his 19-year-old audition issue, replacing one annoying topic with another
jokes.explanation: Good structure — the promise of relief (stopping the Ross/Rachel talk) is immediately undermined by Joey's oblivious pivot. Functional running gag payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa! That is NOT cool. You gotta talk to Rachel. She's your friend. And more importantly, she's my... she's my friend too. So here's what we're gonna do - we're gonna sit down, we're gonna have some coffee, and we're gonna work this out. Word to your mother!

jokes.text: "Seriously? Seriously, no. Okay? You can play your own age, which is 31." / "I'm 30!" / "Joey, you are not. You're 31." / "Oh, crap!"
jokes.setup: Joey insists he can pass for 19; Chandler tells him he should play his actual age of 31
jokes.punchline: Joey doesn't know he's 31 — he thought he was 30 — and his horrified 'Oh, crap!' when corrected treats learning your own age as devastating news
jokes.explanation: Excellent Joey joke. The revelation that he doesn't know his own age is perfectly in character for someone so unconcerned with self-reflection. 'Oh, crap!' is the ideal reaction — genuine distress at learning he's a year older than he thought. High character integration because only Joey would have this specific problem. The beat where Chandler has to correct him is a great comedic straight-man moment.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Would she? Would she? Would she? Would she? Wood she? Wood cheese?

jokes.text: I'm 30! / Joey, you are not. You're 31. / Oh, crap!
jokes.setup: Chandler tells Joey he looks 31
jokes.punchline: Joey corrects him ('I'm 30!'), Chandler insists he's 31, and Joey's reaction — 'Oh, crap!' — reveals he genuinely didn't know his own age
jokes.explanation: Exceptional character joke. 'Oh, crap!' as Joey's reaction to learning his own age is perfectly in character — it's not just that he's trying to seem young, he genuinely didn't know. This is the kind of joke that only works with a character this specific. Very economical, very funny, highly quotable. Close to the 8-anchor quality benchmark.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Wood cheese? That's not a real thing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I don't care, I'd eat it. I'd eat anything right now.

jokes.text: "That is whack."
jokes.setup: Monica is upset and storms off; someone offers a platitude
jokes.punchline: Monica co-opts Joey's teenager slang ('whack') to dismiss what's being said to her — an unexpected callback in an entirely different emotional register
jokes.explanation: Smart callback. Monica using Joey's affected teen slang in a moment of genuine anger is funny precisely because it's incongruous. The word does double duty: it's a callback, and it characterizes Monica's anger through the absurdity of the word choice.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm picturing us on a beach in Fiji, the sun setting, soft music playing... Monica in that little black dress... and me just lying there thinking, 'Well, at least the scenery is nice.'

jokes.text: Phoebe's song in the hallway: "Whenever I get married / Guess who won't be asked to sing / Somebody named Geller / And somebody else named Bing"
jokes.setup: Phoebe has been denied the chance to play at the wedding; she retreats to the hallway with her guitar
jokes.punchline: She processes her rejection by writing and immediately performing a song specifically about the people who rejected her, naming them directly
jokes.explanation: The concept of Phoebe using her musical gift as immediate emotional processing/revenge is very funny and character-specific. 'Somebody named Geller / And somebody else named Bing' is a good lyric — passive-aggressive while technically not naming names.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Your eyes are too wise.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Too wise?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, you have too much wisdom in your eyes. You look old.

jokes.text: "You ate my candy bar!"
jokes.setup: Joey was given Monica's Three Musketeers bar at the start of the episode
jokes.punchline: Phoebe belatedly discovers her candy bar has been eaten — the callback lands as a sudden isolated complaint in an otherwise dramatic conversation
jokes.explanation: The callback to the candy bar works as a tone-break joke — dropping into petty candy grievances in the middle of dramatic relationship conversations is a classic Friends rhythm. Not particularly clever but well-timed.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm not a thunder stealer! I just... I have a lot of embarrassing memories from my teenage years that tend to come up at inopportune moments.

jokes.text: Rachel comes back after the Monica confrontation: "Hey, I just realized we kind of left some stuff up in the air."
jokes.setup: Rachel was in a nearly-sexual situation with Ross that was interrupted by Monica
jokes.punchline: She returns and frames 'will we have sex tonight' as casually as returning to an unfinished business meeting — 'stuff up in the air'
jokes.explanation: The euphemistic 'stuff up in the air' is mildly funny but the joke is a little too restrained to generate a big laugh. It works as a character moment showing Rachel's directness but doesn't have a sharp punchline.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I was just trying to help! The caricaturist was making everyone look ridiculous.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's what caricaturists do, Ross! And he was amazing. He made me look like a beautiful woman with a huge forehead.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not amazing, Monica, that's accurate.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, I thought it was great! I'm keeping that drawing forever.

jokes.text: "Am I going to let you watch me? No."
jokes.setup: Rachel needs to change and Ross is in the room, apparently making no move to leave
jokes.punchline: Rachel answers her own rhetorical question with a flat 'No' — the self-answered question format is a dry comedic beat that implies Ross was at least considering staying
jokes.explanation: Functional quick joke. The self-answered question is a decent format but nothing exceptional. Gets a small laugh from the implication that Ross's hesitation was noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Hey! Hey! You're a mime! You're a mime!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: The romantic moment is over.

jokes.text: Chandler motivates Monica with the honeymoon: "maybe in Paris" / "We will take a moonlit walk on the Rue de la blah-blah-blah."
jokes.setup: Chandler is trying to coax Monica out of her funk by painting a picture of their romantic Paris honeymoon
jokes.punchline: 'Rue de la blah-blah-blah' — Chandler's French evaporates mid-sentence and he replaces it with onomatopoeia, revealing that his romantic vision has very fuzzy geographic details
jokes.explanation: Charming and very Chandler. The collapse from genuine romantic rhetoric into 'blah-blah-blah' is both funny and oddly endearing — it shows sincerity without pretension. 'Rue de la blah-blah-blah' is a genuinely memorable phrase.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: She's just jealous because I'm getting married first and she can't stand that I'm going to be the center of attention for once in my life.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: And if she tries to show me up, I will bring up the time she gained fifteen pounds and couldn't fit into her pants.

jokes.text: "We will sprinkle rose petals on the bed and make love... not just because it's romantic, but because I can."
jokes.setup: Chandler is painting a romantic Paris honeymoon picture to restore Monica's mood
jokes.punchline: 'Not just because it's romantic, but because I can' — Chandler smugly vows to prove his potency on the honeymoon, turning a romantic speech into a personal victory announcement
jokes.explanation: Excellent callback structure. The romantic speech unexpectedly pivots to a confident declaration about his erection as future proof of concept. 'Because I can' transforms the ED storyline into a motivational arc, and the confidence is funny precisely because we've seen his vulnerability earlier. The juxtaposition — rose petals / 'because I can' — is sharp and well-earned.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh, so now I'm the problem? Fine! You know what? I'm going to have sex on this couch!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm going to have sex in this chair!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm going to have sex in the kitchen on the counter!

jokes.text: Chandler: "Don't say anything, you might scare it away." / "It's Paris. Who knows we're here?"
jokes.setup: Phoebe has just appeared at the door interrupting the romantic Paris fantasy
jokes.punchline: Chandler dryly notes that Paris is apparently not remote enough to avoid Phoebe — the joke is that his imagined romantic escape has been colonized by their social circle
jokes.explanation: Solid deadpan callback to the Paris speech. The implication that Phoebe is inescapable — even in imagination — is a good line. Chandler's resignation is funny.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I can't believe you guys are going to have sex on your engagement night.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Well, we're not actually.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Chandler has erectile dysfunction.

jokes.text: Phoebe asks Monica and Chandler for a 'deposit' and 'good-faith money' to 'hold the date' for their wedding
jokes.setup: Monica told Phoebe she could sing at the wedding
jokes.punchline: Phoebe treats the promise like a formal business transaction, demanding a deposit to hold her date — operating as if she's a professional vendor being solicited
jokes.explanation: Funny concept — Phoebe has fully professionalized her friendship obligations. 'Good-faith money to hold the date' implies she has multiple offers she might otherwise accept. Character-specific absurdism.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh yeah, oh yeah, that's right!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh, oh, oh!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes, yes, YES!

jokes.text: Joey comforts Phoebe after rejection: "They break your heart, don't they?" / "You know, I don't really need their permission. You want to sing at their wedding, sing at their wedding."
jokes.setup: Phoebe is dejected after Monica and Chandler refuse to give her a deposit
jokes.punchline: Joey delivers empowerment advice that amounts to 'do it anyway without permission' — his solution to all problems is apparently unilateral action
jokes.explanation: Joey's philosophy of just doing things regardless of permission is consistent with his earlier 'I did it anyway' advice. A milder joke in the same character vein. Functional but not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh, so you two are back together? That's great! I'm so happy for you! You know what? I'm going to remember this moment. And in about five years, when I do something really great, I'm going to expect you both to be just as excited for me. And if you're not, I'm going to be very, very upset. Actually, you know what? I'm going to steal your thunder anyway.

jokes.text: They break your heart, don't they? / You know, I don't really need their permission.
jokes.setup: Phoebe is dejected after being denied a deposit
jokes.punchline: Joey points out she doesn't need permission to sing at a wedding — an epiphany that reframes Phoebe's entire approach to the situation
jokes.explanation: Decent setup for the upcoming escalation. 'They break your heart, don't they?' from Joey is a nice bit of unearned wisdom. Functional transitional joke.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Monica, you're not exactly in a position to get pregnant.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What? Why not?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Because you'd have to actually have sex with Chandler first.

jokes.text: Joey tells Phoebe to fix her eyes for the audition: "Put some tea bags on them for 15 minutes. That'll get rid of your wisdom?" / "Maybe 10 minutes for you."
jokes.setup: Joey tells Phoebe her eyes 'give her away' because they have too much wisdom in them, and tea bags will help
jokes.punchline: 'Maybe 10 minutes for you' implies Phoebe has less wisdom in her eyes than a standard person — her seeming naivety requires less de-wisdomizing time
jokes.explanation: The whole sequence is delightfully absurd — Joey's theory that wisdom lives in the eyes and can be extracted with tea bags is perfect Joey pseudo-science. The '10 minutes for you' tag is a good button that doubles as an affectionate insult to Phoebe.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I kissed him because I needed to know if there was still something there, okay? And Monica does this thing where she just rebounds with whoever's around, and I didn't want to be that person.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I do not rebound!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You rebounded with like five guys after Richard.

jokes.text: "Give her the deposit, give her the ring. I don't care."
jokes.setup: Chandler is frustrated by the Phoebe deposit situation while also dealing with Monica's anger
jokes.punchline: He extends his indifference to 'give her the ring' — his engagement ring — placing zero monetary/sentimental value on it in a moment of exasperation
jokes.explanation: The escalation from 'deposit' to 'engagement ring' is a quick, funny bit of Chandler exhaustion. Good economy but slightly throwaway.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: She chose me.

jokes.text: What a great apology. And you accept it. Bye-bye.
jokes.setup: Ross comes to apologize to Monica but immediately asks what she meant by 'especially you'
jokes.punchline: Monica sarcastically calls it 'a great apology' — noting he's turned it into a question about himself — then dismisses him with 'bye-bye'
jokes.explanation: Monica's sarcastic 'What a great apology' is well-delivered wit, and 'bye-bye' as a dismissal is a nice touch of condescension. The joke works because Ross has completely walked into it.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You missed your chance with me, Rachel. We had our moment.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: It's not going to happen again. I'm with Monica now, and these bad boys are off the market.

jokes.text: "Let's just say it's not the first time you've stolen my thunder. / My sweet 16. You went to third base with my cousin Charlie."
jokes.setup: Ross presses Monica on what she meant by 'especially you' stealing her thunder
jokes.punchline: Monica reveals the history goes back to her sweet 16, when Ross's sexual encounter with her cousin Charlie overshadowed the party — a 20-year-old grievance Ross apparently didn't know was still active
jokes.explanation: Excellent use of off-screen history for character-based comedy. The specificity ('third base,' 'cousin Charlie,' 'sweet 16') makes the joke feel real rather than generic. It reframes Monica's entire character through her deep capacity for holding grudges while also retroactively indicting Ross. The pattern — Ross has been a thunder-stealer his whole life — is both funny and revealing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Okay, Phoebe, what if I told you that Monica and I want you to sing at our vow renewal ceremony?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Really?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No. No, I'm bribing you to stop singing right now.

jokes.text: "The only reason I did that was because your party was so boring. We had a caricaturist."
jokes.setup: Monica accuses Ross of ruining her sweet 16 by going to third base with her cousin
jokes.punchline: Ross defends going to third base with Monica's cousin at her birthday party... by blaming the entertainment choices. 'We had a caricaturist' is the punchline — implying a caricaturist is so boring it justified any behavior
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's funniest lines. The defense is so absurd yet so perfectly in character for Ross — he genuinely believes poor party planning partially exonerates him. 'We had a caricaturist' is an oddly specific, completely irrelevant detail that reframes the whole accusation hilariously. The implication that a caricaturist is insufficient entertainment to prevent acts of sexual opportunism is both funny and a surprisingly sharp character indictment. Highly quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: ♪ Oh, a tiny little man, and he wore a tiny little hat ♪

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Okay, Phoebe, that's enough.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: ♪ And he had a tiny little... ♪

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Phoebe!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? I'm just trying to help!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: When I get my hands on you, Chandler Bing, I am gonna kill you.

jokes.text: Phoebe's revenge song from the hallway: "Whenever I get married / Guess who won't be asked to sing / Somebody named Geller / And somebody else named Bing"
jokes.setup: Phoebe has been shut out of the wedding singing conversation and retreats to the hallway
jokes.punchline: She performs a pointed revenge song specifically naming the people who wronged her — now targeting Ross and Monica's argument as well
jokes.explanation: Second verse of the revenge song running gag. Slightly diminished return on the concept but still charming. The name-dropping of Geller and Bing in song is funny in its passive-aggressive specificity.

jokes.text: "Got me. Easy, mimey, the moment has passed. It ain't gonna happen."
jokes.setup: Monica has pressured Ross to admit he kissed Rachel; she asks why else he'd do it
jokes.punchline: Ross's admission 'Got me' followed by his attempt to shut down the moment with 'easy, mimey' and 'it ain't gonna happen' — the slang and the deflection together characterize Ross's flustered discomfort
jokes.explanation: Mildly funny but primarily a plot beat. 'Easy, mimey' is a funny phrase but the moment doesn't have a strong comedic construction — it's Ross being flustered, which is reliable but unremarkable.

jokes.text: "Rachel, I've been thinking. I don't think us getting together tonight is such a good idea. I'm calling it off." / "Way to save your dignity, my man."
jokes.setup: Ross announces to Joey that he's 'calling off' the almost-sex with Rachel after Monica interrupted
jokes.punchline: Joey's 'way to save your dignity, my man' correctly identifies that Ross is pretending he had a choice in the matter — the encounter was already dead, so his 'calling it off' is pure face-saving
jokes.explanation: Joey cuts through Ross's self-delusion with perfect precision. 'Way to save your dignity' is a great line — it's simultaneously congratulatory and completely withering. Joey's comedic function as the person who states obvious truths obliviously works perfectly here.

jokes.text: Monica tells Rachel: "Maybe you thought you'd get married first. Maybe you can't stand... that your formerly fat friend is getting married first."
jokes.setup: Monica is accusing Rachel of ruining her night out of resentment
jokes.punchline: 'Formerly fat friend' — Monica drops her own weight history as a weapon, suggesting Rachel can't stand that the previously overweight friend won the marriage race
jokes.explanation: Monica weaponizing her own past weight is a surprising and very specific comedic choice. It's dark in the best sitcom way — she's using her own vulnerability as an attack. 'Formerly fat friend' as a self-identifier in the heat of an argument is startling and funny.

jokes.text: "Oh, wow, that... You know what? That is so unfair. Now I want to steal your thunder. Come on, Ross. Let's go have sex!"
jokes.setup: Monica has played the 'formerly fat friend' card; Rachel is hurt and angry
jokes.punchline: Rachel's escalation from wounded dignity to 'Come on, Ross, let's go have sex!' as deliberate thunder-theft is both absurd and hilarious — she commits fully to the most extreme response available
jokes.explanation: The commitment to the bit is what makes it land. Rachel's decision to weaponize sex as a thunder-stealing device is an extreme and perfectly logical escalation within the episode's internal rules. The audience has been primed for this. Ross's reaction — presumably horrified/excited — would add to the impact in the room.

jokes.text: "I can't believe you're gonna have sex on my engagement night." / "Well, somebody should."
jokes.setup: Rachel dramatically announces she and Ross will go have sex; Monica is offended
jokes.punchline: 'Well, somebody should' — Rachel's callback to Chandler's erectile dysfunction shuts Monica down while simultaneously referencing the bedroom failure, delivering maximum damage in two words
jokes.explanation: The episode's best joke. 'Well, somebody should' is a perfect three-word callback that does multiple things simultaneously: it references Chandler's ED without naming it, it twists the knife on Monica, it's Rachel at her most wickedly sharp, and the economy is flawless. The structure earns a 9 because it requires the whole episode's setup — Chandler's ED arc — to pay off this cleanly. This is the kind of punchline that gets an enormous studio laugh and plays even better on rewatch when you catch all the layers. Closest to the anchor examples in quality.

jokes.text: "Look, if we're gonna do this..." / "We're not. She's just gonna think we are." / "I see, so everybody wins."
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel retreat to fake having sex to spite Monica
jokes.punchline: Ross's 'I see, so everybody wins' — delivered as if he's been cheated — reveals he was actually hoping the fake sex plan was real
jokes.explanation: Ross's quietly crestfallen 'everybody wins' is a good character joke. The sarcasm is mild but the implication — that he was hoping this would go somewhere — is funny and very Ross.

jokes.text: Ross and Rachel fake-moan when Monica knocks: "Yeah, you like that, baby?"
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel have agreed to fake having sex to mess with Monica; Monica knocks
jokes.punchline: Ross immediately produces the most generic, over-the-top dirty talk — 'Yeah, you like that, baby?' — an absurd choice that's both committed and deeply uncool
jokes.explanation: The joke is partly in the specific phrase Ross chooses — it's so generic and try-hard that it characterizes him perfectly. The commitment to the bit (they went through with the fake sex noise plan) is funnier than any specific line. Big reaction expected from live audience.

jokes.text: Monica enters to find Ross and Rachel mid-fake-sex: "May we help you?"
jokes.setup: Monica walks in on what appears to be Ross and Rachel having sex
jokes.punchline: 'May we help you?' — delivered as if Monica has interrupted a business meeting rather than a sexual encounter, maximum deadpan in an absurd situation
jokes.explanation: The formal register of 'May we help you?' in a fake sex context is a good deadpan choice. Very economical — four words that say everything. The visual of whoever is delivering this line in an obviously staged position would amplify the laugh significantly.

jokes.text: Monica: "I wanted to say I hope you have sex, and I hope you get back together. I warn you, the night you announce your engagement... I'm going to announce that I'm pregnant."
jokes.setup: Monica walks in on the fake sex; rather than being embarrassed, she makes a declaration
jokes.punchline: Monica pre-announces her counter-thunder-theft — she's already planning her revenge announcement for their future engagement night, turning this into an ongoing thunder war
jokes.explanation: Monica's strategic long-game retaliation is excellent character comedy. She's already planning for a hypothetical future engagement so she can steal their thunder back. The escalation from 'tonight' to 'whenever you get engaged' reveals Monica's grudge architecture. 'How is that ever going to happen?' is a good button.

jokes.text: "How is that ever going to happen?"
jokes.setup: Monica threatens to announce a pregnancy on the night they announce an engagement
jokes.punchline: Either Rachel or Ross points out the obvious problem: they'd need to actually get engaged for this threat to matter — a dig at their perpetual romantic limbo
jokes.explanation: Good quick button on the Monica thunder-revenge threat. The self-deprecating acknowledgment that Ross and Rachel may never get engaged is a nice layer. Functional.

jokes.text: How is that ever going to happen?
jokes.setup: Monica threatens to announce a pregnancy to steal their future thunder
jokes.punchline: Ross's question — 'How is that ever going to happen?' — implying Monica and Chandler won't be able to have children, or more immediately, that Chandler can't perform sexually
jokes.explanation: Another callback to Chandler's performance issue. Ross's question works because it functions on two levels — the surface reading (a fertility question) and the subtext (Chandler can't perform). Clean economy.

jokes.text: "You know, I'm so... so happy for you guys. But you getting married reminds me of the fact that I'm not. I'm not even close." / "I know that that's dumb, but you were so depressed... when Ross got married, you slept with Chandler."
jokes.setup: Rachel confesses she kissed Ross because Monica's engagement reminded her she's alone
jokes.punchline: Rachel's sincere emotional confession is immediately interrupted by her blurting out that Monica, when similarly depressed about Ross's wedding, slept with Chandler — weaponizing Monica's own romantic history to make herself feel better
jokes.explanation: The pivot from Rachel's sincere vulnerability to 'you slept with Chandler' is sharp — it draws the parallel between their situations in a way that's simultaneously empathetic and funny. It also retroactively recontextualizes Chandler and Monica's relationship origin as Monica's rebound hookup, which is both dark and very funny. Good character integration.

jokes.text: "I don't care, she slept with me."
jokes.setup: Rachel has just said Monica slept with Chandler out of depression when Ross got married
jokes.punchline: Chandler's interjection — 'I don't care, she slept with me' — reframes the narrative entirely, staking his claim as the beneficiary of the transaction regardless of Monica's motivations
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's top three jokes. Six words, enormous laugh. Chandler's breezy dismissal of the framing — he doesn't care WHY Monica slept with him, only THAT she did — is delivered with perfect confidence. The joke works on multiple levels: it's self-aware about the questionable origin of their relationship, it's delivered from complete contentment, and 'I don't care, she slept with me' as a philosophy of life is both funny and oddly endearing. Near-perfect economy.

jokes.text: Monica: "I'm sorry I almost made you sleep with Ross."
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are having a sincere reconciliation moment
jokes.punchline: Monica's apology includes apologizing for almost making Rachel sleep with Ross — treating potential Ross-sex as a harm she almost inflicted on her friend
jokes.explanation: Funny because it treats Ross-sex as a negative outcome Monica needs to apologize for — which retroactively roasts Ross while also winking at Rachel's complicated Ross history. The apologetic framing is both touching and subtly devastating to Ross.

jokes.text: Ross to Rachel after the reconciliation: "And Rachel... what can I say? You missed your chance. From now on, the only person who's going to enjoy these bad boys is me."
jokes.setup: Everyone has reconciled; Ross enters to deliver a final word to Rachel
jokes.punchline: 'These bad boys' — Ross referring to his hands with supreme confidence, calling back to Rachel's earlier 'I really liked your hands' and transforming a mild compliment into a declaration of sexual self-ownership
jokes.explanation: Excellent callback construction. 'These bad boys' referring to Ross's hands calls back to Rachel's earlier fumbling compliment, but now delivered with absurd self-satisfaction. The fact that Ross's greatest romantic asset is his hands — something Rachel struggled to even name — and he's now strutting about them is very funny. The callback elevates both jokes retroactively.

jokes.text: Phoebe's final song: "We thought Phoebe would leave / But she just stayed and stayed / That's right, I'm here all night / And Chandler will never get..." (interrupted by Chandler paying her a dollar)
jokes.setup: Phoebe has been playing songs throughout the episode; she now launches into one about the whole night, clearly about to reference Chandler's ED
jokes.punchline: Chandler immediately bribes her with a dollar to stop — before she can finish 'Chandler will never get...' — and the payment comes faster than any other negotiation in the episode
jokes.explanation: Perfect running-gag payoff. Chandler's immediate cave — paying the deposit he denied earlier — shows how much his sexual vulnerability has become his Achilles heel by episode's end. The song cuts off at exactly the right moment and Chandler's desperation to stop it is funnier than any explicit reference to his ED would be. Good episode-closing joke that wraps multiple threads.

jokes.text: Hey, here's a dollar. Consider it a deposit. Please sing at our wedding.
jokes.setup: Phoebe's song is heading somewhere embarrassing for Chandler; he needs to stop it
jokes.punchline: Chandler pays Phoebe a dollar deposit to officially engage her as the wedding singer — essentially bribing her to stop singing right now
jokes.explanation: Perfect running gag payoff. The entire episode's thread of Phoebe demanding a deposit is resolved by Chandler caving — not out of generosity but out of self-preservation. 'Here's a dollar' as the final settlement of a multiple-episode running negotiation is funny in its scale mismatch. Well-structured closing beat.

jokes.text: "Now who will perform the ceremony / Who will perform the cer..." (Chandler to Monica) / "I'll pound on him in the morning."
jokes.setup: Phoebe, now paid and emboldened, immediately starts a new verse asking who will perform the ceremony
jokes.punchline: Monica's resigned 'I'll pound on him in the morning' — echoing her earlier threat about Phoebe — signals that she's given up fighting and will deal with Phoebe's escalating demands tomorrow
jokes.explanation: Good final button on the episode. The callback to Monica's earlier 'pound on him' threat closes the Phoebe-wedding arc neatly. Monica's weary acceptance is a satisfying character note to end on.

jokes.text: I'll pound on him in the morning.
jokes.setup: Phoebe is immediately escalating to wanting to perform the ceremony; Monica and Chandler presumably just want their night back
jokes.punchline: Monica repeats her earlier threat to 'pound on' someone — this time directed at Chandler, who has just paid Phoebe the deposit and enabled this new round of Phoebe's demands
jokes.explanation: Decent callback closer. Monica threatening to pound Chandler rather than Phoebe is a fun reversal — she's directing her frustration at the enabler. 'In the morning' as a qualifier (they still have their romantic night ahead) is a nice touch.

tmdb_overview: The gang celebrate Monica and Chandler's engagement. Phoebe wants to be the musician at the wedding and comes up with a new song, while Joey tries to dress and act like a 19-year-old for an audition. Ross and Rachel briefly reunite and after Monica catches them kissing, she's convinced that Rachel is trying to steal her thunder.
insight: Season opener resets cast dynamics but lands below-average 71 score with thin standout moments.
